params.question: Why should hypertensive disorders of pregnancy be understood as a continuum rather than as separate, discrete conditions?

answers.text: All forms of HDP share identical histological changes in the placenta

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Different subtypes of HDP have distinct pathological mechanisms. The continuum concept refers to clinical progression, not shared histology.

answers.text: A woman can rapidly progress from a milder to a more severe category, making early recognition essential

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. A woman with apparently mild gestational hypertension can deteriorate rapidly into severe pre-eclampsia or eclampsia. Viewing HDP as a spectrum encourages vigilant monitoring at every stage.

answers.text: The same antihypertensive drug is effective across all categories of HDP

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While some drugs are used across categories, treatment is tailored to severity. The continuum concept refers to the potential for disease progression, not uniformity of treatment.

answers.text: Proteinuria is invariably present from the earliest stage of the disorder

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Proteinuria is a feature of pre-eclampsia but is absent in gestational hypertension. The continuum concept is about the potential for progression between categories, not about shared clinical features.

overallFeedback.feedback: HDP is best viewed as a continuum because patients can progress rapidly from milder to more severe forms. This understanding is critical for timely recognition and intervention.
Well done. Recognising HDP as a continuum ensures you remain vigilant for deterioration even when the initial presentation appears mild.

params.question: Why is a structured antenatal screening protocol considered essential for detecting gestational diabetes mellitus?

answers.text: GDM causes obvious glycosuria that is easily detected on routine urinalysis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Glycosuria in pregnancy can occur physiologically due to a lowered renal glucose threshold and is not a reliable indicator of GDM.

answers.text: GDM is typically asymptomatic and cannot be reliably detected without laboratory testing

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Most women with GDM have no symptoms at all. Polyuria and polydipsia, when present, are non-specific and unreliable. Only systematic laboratory screening ensures timely detection and intervention.

answers.text: Screening is needed only for women with a family history of diabetes mellitus

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: GDM screening should be universal, not restricted to high-risk groups. Many women who develop GDM have no identifiable risk factors.

answers.text: The glucose tolerance test must be repeated each trimester to be accurate

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The reason screening is essential is that GDM is clinically silent, not that the test requires repetition. The protocol defines specific timing for screening.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key reason is that GDM is typically asymptomatic. Occasional symptoms such as polyuria are non-specific and unreliable, making structured laboratory screening the only dependable method of detection.
Exactly. GDM is a silent condition — without a systematic screening protocol, affected pregnancies would go undetected and untreated.

params.question: A 28-year-old woman at 35 weeks with severe pre-eclampsia has been stabilised with antihypertensives and MgSO₄. Which principle should guide the next management decision?

answers.text: Continue antihypertensives and MgSO₄ indefinitely, as they will eventually resolve the underlying disease

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Antihypertensives and MgSO₄ are temporising measures — they control symptoms but do not treat the underlying placental pathology driving pre-eclampsia.

answers.text: Plan for delivery, as removal of the placenta is the only definitive treatment for pre-eclampsia

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Pre-eclampsia is driven by placental factors. Antihypertensives prevent end-organ damage and MgSO₄ prevents seizures, but only delivery of the placenta halts the disease process.

answers.text: Discontinue MgSO₄ once blood pressure is controlled, as it is only needed during acute hypertensive episodes

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: MgSO₄ is an anticonvulsant, not an antihypertensive. It is continued for seizure prophylaxis independently of blood pressure control.

answers.text: Delay delivery until 40 weeks to ensure fetal lung maturity, regardless of the maternal condition

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While fetal maturity is considered, maternal safety takes precedence. In severe pre-eclampsia at 35 weeks, the risk of continuing the pregnancy often outweighs the benefit of expectant management.

overallFeedback.feedback: The critical principle is that delivery of the placenta is the only definitive treatment for pre-eclampsia. All other interventions — antihypertensives, MgSO₄ — stabilise the mother while the team prepares for delivery.
Correct. Internalising that delivery is the only definitive cure guides the team to treat BP and seizures as temporising steps while planning safe delivery.

interactions.label: A primigravida at 36 weeks has newly detected BP of 148/96 mmHg with no proteinu

params.question: A primigravida at 36 weeks has newly detected BP of 148/96 mmHg with no proteinuria. Considering the complete clinical arc of HDP, which approach is MOST justified?

answers.text: Immediate delivery, because all hypertensive disorders ultimately require placental removal

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While delivery is definitive for pre-eclampsia, mild gestational hypertension at 36 weeks does not mandate immediate delivery. Premature intervention is not justified when the clinical arc has not yet progressed to that stage.

answers.text: Enhanced surveillance with serial BP monitoring, proteinuria screening, and fetal assessment, because HDP can escalate rapidly

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The clinical arc teaches that HDP is a continuum — mild gestational hypertension can progress to pre-eclampsia. Enhanced surveillance detects deterioration early while avoiding premature intervention.

answers.text: Reassurance and routine follow-up only, since the absence of proteinuria rules out pre-eclampsia

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Absence of proteinuria at one time point does not exclude future progression to pre-eclampsia. The continuum nature of HDP demands heightened vigilance, not false reassurance.

answers.text: Start MgSO₄ prophylaxis immediately to prevent potential eclamptic seizures

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: MgSO₄ is indicated for seizure prophylaxis in severe pre-eclampsia or eclampsia, not for mild gestational hypertension. Applying it here would be disproportionate to the clinical stage.

overallFeedback.feedback: The clinical arc of HDP teaches that it is a continuum with potential for rapid progression. At this early stage, the justified response is enhanced surveillance — not premature delivery, false reassurance, or disproportionate treatment.
Excellent. Applying the complete clinical arc means recognising that even mild HDP warrants enhanced surveillance — balancing vigilance against premature intervention.
